### Purpose Statement

This standard profile defines how AWS API Management implementations conform to existing enterprise API, security, and operations standards.
page_texts.6:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#scope]

### Scope

This profile applies to application teams and platform teams deploying API Management capabilities on AWS services, including gateway ingress, identity integration, policy enforcement, and observability.

**Responsibility Boundaries:** Controls referenced in this profile are owned at two distinct tiers. The table below clarifies accountability to prevent misalignment between teams.

| Control Area | Owner | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API contract authoring and lifecycle | Application Team | Style-appropriate contract creation (OpenAPI 3.x mandatory for REST per Requirement 4; other styles per Q11 of GUID-APP-IMPL-010), versioning, CI/CD validation |
| Business logic and service instrumentation | Application Team | OTel SDK integration for Kubernetes/EKS-deployed services (proposed, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification — see Requirement 3); Lambda/ECS-deployed services follow the CloudWatch/X-Ray AWS-native baseline instead; domain service implementation |
| API catalog registration and documentation | Application Team | Catalog entry, ownership metadata, spec publication |
| Shared gateway infrastructure (Amazon API Gateway) | Platform Team | Stage configuration, throttling policies, IaC templates |
| WAF policy and web ACL association | Platform Team | Layer-7 rules, threat rule sets, association to protected stages |
| Enterprise IdP integration and token issuance | Platform Team | Entra ID (Gainwell GPD) / federated IdP configuration, claim mapping |
| OTel Collector infrastructure and enterprise routing | Platform Team | Collector deployment, signal routing to observability backends |
| CloudTrail and SIEM routing | Platform Team | Management-plane audit forwarding, SIEM integration pipelines |

Application teams consume shared platform components via governed onboarding workflows; they do not build or operate platform-owned controls. Security Architecture must confirm boundary assignments for any control not listed here during the formal review gate.
page_texts.7:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#compliance-level]

### Compliance Level

This profile creates no normative authority of its own — it applies obligations already established elsewhere to the AWS context. Its `compliance_level` metadata is `guidance` because the profile document itself is a translation/aggregation layer, not because the requirements it inherits from already-ratified, mandatory sources are non-binding: Requirements 1, 2, 4, and 5 below are enforceable today, exactly as they are in their originating standard or active security control. Where a requirement in this profile is sourced from an artifact that is not itself yet ratified (`status: draft`), this profile states that plainly and marks the requirement as proposed/pending rather than presenting it as a current mandate — see Requirement 3.

**Tiered compliance model in this profile:**

| Tier | Meaning | Examples in this profile |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mandatory (SHALL) — enforceable now | Inherited from an already-ratified (`status: active`) mandatory standard or an active security control | Requirement 1 and Requirement 4 (STD-APP-API-001, `status: active`); Requirement 2 and Requirement 5 (the active AWS security control baseline in GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB) |
| Proposed / Pending — not yet enforceable | Sourced from an artifact that is itself `status: draft`; becomes mandatory under this profile only once that source is ratified | Requirement 3 (OTel instrumentation per STD-APP-MON-002, which is currently `status: draft`) |
| Recommended (SHOULD) | Good practice drawn from guidance-tier artifacts; non-conformance requires documented rationale | Contract-first API definitions; API catalog registration; classification per STD-APP-API-003/004; gateway management practice per STD-APP-API-005; mesh-vs-gateway decision framework per STD-APP-API-006; federated-delivery-with-centralized-shared-controls operating model per GUID-APP-IMPL-010 (Practice 9) |
| Guidance (profile-level) | This document itself; applies referenced obligations to AWS context | STD-APP-API-007 in its entirety |

This profile creates no net-new mandatory controls: every Mandatory-tier item above is already binding through its originating standard or active security control, independent of this profile. Requirement 3 is the sole exception — it previews an obligation this profile will inherit once STD-APP-MON-002 completes ratification, and is not a present mandate.

page_texts.10:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#mandatory-requirements]

### Mandatory Requirements

Implementations SHALL satisfy Requirements 1, 2, 4, and 5 below, each traceable to an already-ratified mandatory standard or an active security control. Requirement 3 is listed here for completeness but is proposed/pending, not a present mandate — see its entry for scope and ratification status. No requirement in this section elevates a guidance-tier artifact to a mandate before that artifact itself is ratified:

- Requirement 1: Conform to API design and contract requirements in [STD-APP-API-001](./STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md) (mandatory).
- Requirement 2: Conform to the AWS network security control baseline in [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) (active Solution Building Block): API Gateway SHALL intercept 100% of API traffic with no direct network path to backend services (REQ-APIGW-01); East-West traffic SHALL receive the same authentication, authorization, and encryption controls as North-South traffic (REQ-APIGW-03); internal-only APIs SHALL be deployed on private, non-internet-routable gateway endpoints (REQ-APIGW-04).
- Requirement 3 (proposed, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification): Once [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) completes Domain EA and Security Architecture ratification (currently `status: draft`), application services deployed on Kubernetes/EKS will be required to instrument with OpenTelemetry, scoped to Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services — legacy non-Kubernetes services remain out of scope pending separate migration guidance. Dynatrace is the primary enterprise APM backend per [ADR-OPS-001](../../../decisions/itsm-operations/ADR-OPS-001-performance-monitoring-strategy.md); AWS-native observability services (CloudWatch, X-Ray) are limited to AWS-native compute resource metrics/logs and do not replace Dynatrace as the primary APM backend or the OTel SDK as the application instrumentation layer. Until ratification, teams are encouraged to instrument proactively, but this requirement does not yet carry mandatory force under this profile.
- Requirement 4: All REST APIs must use OpenAPI Specification 3.x as the contract format per [STD-APP-API-001](./STD-APP-API-001-api-design.md) (mandatory). OpenAPI contracts must be validated in CI/CD prior to deployment.
- Requirement 5: East-West (internal service-to-service) API traffic implemented as a **REST API** SHALL be deployed behind a Private API Gateway (endpoint type `PRIVATE`, reachable only via VPC Endpoint) per the Requirement 2 control baseline (GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB REQ-APIGW-01/03/04). That active SBB's control — API Gateway interception plus private, non-internet-routable gateway endpoints — applies to REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs alike; it carves out no exception by API type. However, Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs do not support a Private (PrivateLink/VPC endpoint) endpoint type and support only Regional (internet-routable) endpoints — there is no technical mechanism by which an HTTP or WebSocket API can satisfy REQ-APIGW-04 as written. This is a genuine, unresolved conflict between the SBB's mandate and Amazon API Gateway's technical capabilities for East-West HTTP/WebSocket traffic. This profile does not have the authority to resolve that conflict and does not authorize any alternative (an internal Application Load Balancer, another private frontend, a VPC Link/NLB integration, or otherwise) as a sanctioned substitute — a VPC Link/NLB integration in particular does not satisfy REQ-APIGW-04 on its own, since it privatizes only the API Gateway-to-backend integration and does not make the HTTP or WebSocket API's own client-facing endpoint non-internet-routable. Until Security Architecture resolves this gap through its SBB exception process or an SBB amendment, teams SHOULD implement East-West traffic as a REST API using the `PRIVATE` endpoint type wherever the API's actual requirements permit it; any East-West HTTP or WebSocket API that cannot be reimplemented as REST is an open compliance gap and SHALL be tracked and remediated through Security Architecture's exception process rather than resolved through a self-approved workaround. Service mesh — selected per the guidance-tier decision framework in [STD-APP-API-006](./STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) — is a permitted complementary control for mTLS and fine-grained service identity between services; it does not substitute for the Private API Gateway's mandatory interception, authorization, and audit-logging responsibilities, and it does not close the SBB gap described above. See Technical Specifications, Requirement Category 2, for the full control statement.
page_texts.11:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#recommended-practices]

### Recommended Practices

The following practices draw on guidance-tier standards (STD-APP-API-003, STD-APP-API-004, STD-APP-API-005, STD-APP-API-006 — all `compliance_level: guidance`) and a Draft security guidance artifact. Non-conformance requires documented rationale but does not constitute a standards violation.

- Practice 1: Use contract-first API definitions and validate them in CI/CD.
- Practice 2: Separate shared platform controls (authn/authz, WAF, logging) from business service logic.
- Practice 3: Publish API onboarding and usage guidance via the developer portal pattern.
- Practice 4: Register all APIs — internal and external — in the enterprise API catalog with lifecycle stage, owner, and a style-appropriate API specification reference (OpenAPI for REST; `.proto`, GraphQL SDL, or AsyncAPI otherwise).
- Practice 5: Follow API Gateway management practice in [STD-APP-API-005](./STD-APP-API-005-api-gateway-management.md) (guidance-tier).
- Practice 6: Classify APIs as internal/external and North-South/East-West per [STD-APP-API-003](./STD-APP-API-003-internal-external-api-guidelines.md) and [STD-APP-API-004](./STD-APP-API-004-north-south-east-west-apis.md) (guidance-tier).
- Practice 7: Apply the mesh-vs-gateway decision framework in [STD-APP-API-006](./STD-APP-API-006-api-mesh-vs-gateway-guidance.md) (guidance-tier) to decide where service mesh complements the mandatory Private API Gateway baseline in Requirement 5.
- Practice 8: Reference [GUID-SEC-INT-API GATEWAY-2.8.01](../../../strategy/guidance/security/integration-security/GUID-SEC-INT-API%20GATEWAY-2.8.01.md) for supplemental API gateway security guidance; this artifact is currently `status: Draft` and is non-normative until approved.
- Practice 9 (recommended, not mandated): Consider a federated-delivery-with-centralized-shared-controls operating model — domain teams own API contracts and lifecycle decisions, while a platform team owns shared gateway, WAF, IdP, and OTel Collector infrastructure — as described in [GUID-APP-IMPL-010](../../../strategy/guidance/application/implementation/GUID-APP-IMPL-010-api-engineering-guidance.md) (guidance-tier, currently `status: draft`). No ratified standard or approved decision record currently mandates this operating model; this profile does not impose it as a Constraint, and teams should not treat it as an enforceable requirement until an accepted ADR or ratified standard authorizes it.
page_texts.12:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#prohibited-practices]

### Prohibited Practices

- Prohibition 1: Bypassing gateway-level policy enforcement for externally consumed APIs.
- Prohibition 2: Deploying APIs without standards-aligned authentication and authorization controls.
- Prohibition 3: Omitting operational logging and audit telemetry required by existing governance and security artifacts.
- Prohibition 4 (proposed, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification): Instrumenting application services with vendor-specific observability SDKs (e.g., AWS X-Ray SDK, CloudWatch Embedded Metrics Format) as a replacement for the OpenTelemetry SDK instrumentation layer. This prohibition inherits its enforceability from Requirement 3 above and does not carry mandatory force under this profile until [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) completes Domain EA and Security Architecture ratification (currently `status: draft`).
  - Clarification: Vendor SDKs and agents may be used as OTel exporters or Collector-side processors. For Kubernetes/EKS-deployed services, the primary application instrumentation layer is intended to be the OpenTelemetry SDK per STD-APP-MON-002 (Requirement 3) — enforceable once that standard completes ratification; Lambda/ECS-deployed services are unaffected by this prohibition and continue to use the CloudWatch/X-Ray AWS-native baseline.
- Prohibition 5: Operating East-West (internal service-to-service) API traffic implemented as a **REST API** without a Private API Gateway control point (endpoint type `PRIVATE`). Service mesh alone, with no gateway interception, does not satisfy REQ-APIGW-01/03/04 of [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md). East-West traffic implemented as an HTTP or WebSocket API is subject to the same SBB mandate but cannot technically satisfy the `PRIVATE` endpoint-type control (see Requirement 5) — this is an unresolved SBB/technical-capability gap, not a sanctioned exception from this prohibition, and any such API SHALL be tracked and remediated through Security Architecture's exception process until the gap is closed.

[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#requirement-category-1-gateway-and-access-controls-north-south-apis]

#### Requirement Category 1: Gateway and Access Controls (North-South APIs)

- Enforce ingress through managed API gateway capabilities for all North-South (external-facing) APIs.
- Integrate enterprise identity provider patterns for token and policy evaluation.
- Apply security protections using approved gateway and network controls.
- APIs must not be exposed directly to external consumers without passing through the managed gateway.
- Backend service integrations from the API Gateway SHALL use HTTPS. HTTP (cleartext) backend integrations are prohibited regardless of VPC Link or private network path configuration — aligns with [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) AD-02 (End-to-End TLS). VPC Link provides network isolation but does not substitute for transport-layer encryption.
page_texts.17:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#requirement-category-2-internal-api-controls-east-west-apis]

#### Requirement Category 2: Internal API Controls (East-West APIs)

- East-West (internal service-to-service) APIs implemented as a **REST API** SHALL be deployed behind a Private API Gateway (endpoint type `PRIVATE`, VPC Endpoint-only access) per [GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB](../../../strategy/guidance/security/Network/GUID-SEC-NETWORK-API-GW-AWS-2.2.04.SSB.md) REQ-APIGW-01/03/04 — API Gateway interception is the mandatory control-plane baseline for internal traffic, not an optional path. That SBB's control — API Gateway interception plus private, non-internet-routable gateway endpoints — applies to REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs alike, with no exception by API type. However, Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs and WebSocket APIs do not support a Private endpoint type and support only Regional (internet-routable) endpoints, so there is no technical mechanism by which an HTTP or WebSocket API can satisfy REQ-APIGW-04 as written. This is an unresolved SBB/technical-capability gap, not a control this profile can close on its own authority: no alternative (an internal Application Load Balancer, another private frontend, a VPC Link/NLB integration, or otherwise) is authorized as a sanctioned substitute — a VPC Link/NLB integration in particular privatizes only the API Gateway-to-backend integration, not the client-facing endpoint. Teams SHOULD implement East-West traffic as a REST API using the `PRIVATE` endpoint type wherever the API's actual requirements permit it; any East-West HTTP or WebSocket API that cannot be reimplemented as REST is an open compliance gap requiring Security Architecture's SBB exception process or an SBB amendment, not a self-approved workaround.
- Where a domain additionally requires mutual TLS (mTLS) and fine-grained service identity between services, layer a service mesh or equivalent control on top of the Private API Gateway baseline; the mesh is complementary, does not substitute for gateway interception, and does not close the SBB gap described above for HTTP/WebSocket East-West traffic.
- Internal APIs SHOULD be classified per [STD-APP-API-003](./STD-APP-API-003-internal-external-api-guidelines.md) and inventoried in the API catalog (Recommended tier — see Recommended Practices 4 and 6; no ratified mandatory source elevates this to a Requirement).
- Refer to [PTN-APP-API-031](../../../patterns/application/api-microservices/PTN-APP-API-031-service-mesh-integration-pattern.md) for service mesh implementation as a complementary control.
page_texts.18:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#requirement-category-3-operations-observability-and-openapi]

#### Requirement Category 3: Operations, Observability, and OpenAPI

- Capture runtime request telemetry and control-plane audit events.
- Instrument application services deployed on Kubernetes/EKS with OpenTelemetry per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md), once that standard completes ratification (currently `status: draft` — see Requirement 3); OTel Collector routes signals to Dynatrace (primary enterprise APM). Lambda- and ECS-deployed services use the CloudWatch/X-Ray AWS-native observability baseline instead.
- Preserve traceability for API lifecycle and policy changes.
- All REST APIs must publish OpenAPI 3.x specifications; validate specs in CI/CD.

### Architecture Constraints

- Constraint 1: AWS-specific implementation choices must remain aligned to enterprise standards and patterns.

page_texts.20:
[standards/application/api/STD-APP-API-007-aws-api-management-standard-profile.md#technology-standards]

### Technology Standards

| Technology | Approved Versions | Configuration Requirements | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Amazon API Gateway | Per enterprise platform baseline | Stage and policy configuration via controlled IaC | Gateway ingress and policy enforcement for North-South (Regional/Edge endpoint) APIs and the mandatory East-West control-plane baseline (Private endpoint type) per Requirement 5 / Category 2 |
| Entra ID (Gainwell GPD) / Federated IdP | Per enterprise identity baseline | Token and claim validation integrated at gateway via Lambda authorizer | Identity and access control |
| AWS WAF | Per enterprise security baseline | REST APIs: direct Web ACL association to the protected API stage. HTTP/WebSocket APIs: direct stage-level Web ACL association is not supported — front the API with Amazon CloudFront or an Application Load Balancer and associate the Web ACL there instead (consistent with [REF-APP-API-001](../../../strategy/reference/application/REF-APP-API-001-aws-api-management-reference-architecture.md)) | Layer-7 protections; direct stage-level Web ACL association is a REST-API-only capability |
| OpenTelemetry SDK + OTel Collector | Per [STD-APP-MON-002](../../../standards/application/monitoring/STD-APP-MON-002-opentelemetry-observability.md) | OTel SDK in Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services; Collector routes to Dynatrace (primary enterprise APM) | **Proposed for Kubernetes/EKS-deployed application services, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification (Requirement 3)** |
| CloudWatch / CloudTrail | Per enterprise observability baseline | AWS-native compute resource metrics/logs (Lambda, ECS) and management-plane telemetry | AWS-native backend — supplements, does not replace, Dynatrace APM |
| OpenAPI Specification 3.x | 3.0+ | Contract-first authoring; CI/CD validation required | Mandatory REST API contract format |

## Change History

| Date | Version | Author | Description | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-14 | 1.0.10 | GitHub Copilot | Relabeled the Examples and References → Implementation Examples (Example 1/2), which presented "Compliance Evidence"/"Lessons Learned" as if observed/evidenced outcomes despite no traceable real-world implementation evidence existing anywhere in this artifact suite (per GUID-APP-IMPL-011's own Change History) — same defect class as GUID-APP-IMPL-009's round-16 Finding 5; added an explanatory illustrative-outcomes note and reworded the fields to "Expected Evidence"/"Expected Lessons" | PR #249 review remediation, round 17 |
| 2026-09-14 | 1.0.9 | GitHub Copilot | Corrected Requirement 5 and Requirement Category 2: removed the prior round's unauthorized framing that a "separately Security Architecture-approved private frontend/control design" is an already-enforceable `SHALL` alternative for East-West HTTP/WebSocket APIs — the cited active SBB requires API Gateway interception plus private, non-internet-routable endpoints for REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs alike and authorizes no ALB/other-frontend equivalent; reframed this as a genuine, unresolved SBB/technical-capability gap (no `PRIVATE` endpoint type exists for HTTP/WebSocket APIs) requiring Security Architecture's SBB exception process or an SBB amendment, not a profile-sanctioned substitute; realigned Prohibition 5 to the same REST-scoped mandatory control / HTTP-WebSocket-gap framing so it no longer contradicts Requirement 5; qualified the AWS WAF Technology Standards row to note that direct Web ACL-to-stage association is a REST-API-only capability and that HTTP/WebSocket APIs require a CloudFront- or ALB-fronted WAF equivalent, consistent with REF-APP-API-001 | PR #249 review remediation, round 16 |
| 2026-09-14 | 1.0.8 | GitHub Copilot | Scoped Requirement 5's and Requirement Category 2's `PRIVATE` endpoint-type mandate explicitly to REST APIs (HTTP/WebSocket APIs do not support that endpoint type); added a routed equivalent-control path (REST API re-platform or a separately Security Architecture-approved private frontend/control design) for East-West HTTP/WebSocket APIs, and clarified that VPC Link/NLB alone does not satisfy the private-endpoint control; demoted the Requirement Category 2 API classification/catalog-registration mandate from "must" to "SHOULD" to resolve its contradiction with Recommended Practices 4 and 6, which already classify both as non-mandatory | PR #249 review remediation, round 15 |
| 2026-09-14 | 1.0.7 | GitHub Copilot | Marked Prohibition 4 (OTel-replacement prohibition) as "proposed, pending STD-APP-MON-002 ratification" in its own heading rather than only in its clarification, so it is not read as a current enforceable prohibition; removed Constraint 4 (federated-delivery-with-centralized-shared-controls operating model) from Architecture Constraints — no ratified standard or accepted ADR currently authorizes it as a mandate, only the draft GUID-APP-IMPL-010 guidance and the new draft white paper — and republished it as Recommended Practice 9 (non-mandatory), with a corresponding Recommended-tier example added to the Compliance Level table | PR #249 review remediation, round 8 |
| 2026-09-11 | 1.0.6 | GitHub Copilot | Reframed the Compliance Level section so it no longer claims the whole artifact is non-mandatory guidance while its own Mandatory Requirements section states SHALL obligations — clarified that Requirements 1, 2, 4, and 5 are enforceable now (inherited from already-ratified sources) while Requirement 3 is proposed/pending because its source, STD-APP-MON-002, is itself `status: draft`; propagated the same Requirement 3 pending-ratification framing to the Responsibility Boundaries table, Requirement Category 3, the Technology Standards table, the Prohibition 4 clarification, and the Related Standards bullet so the document no longer contradicts itself | PR #249 review remediation, round 5 |
| 2026-09-11 | 1.0.5 | GitHub Copilot | Qualified the Responsibility Boundaries table's API contract and instrumentation rows to match the scoping already established in the Requirements section (OpenAPI 3.x mandatory for REST per Requirement 4; OTel SDK mandatory for Kubernetes/EKS per Requirement 3), preventing non-REST and Lambda/ECS implementations from being assigned the wrong obligations; updated the GUID-APP-API-002 cross-reference to its renamed ID GUID-APP-IMPL-010 | PR #249 review remediation, round 4 |
| 2026-09-11 | 1.0.4 | GitHub Copilot | Qualified the remaining unqualified STD-APP-MON-002 Related Standards bullet to Kubernetes/EKS + CloudWatch/X-Ray, matching the already-corrected Requirement Category 3 wording | PR #249 review remediation, round 3 |
| 2026-09-11 | 1.0.3 | GitHub Copilot | Corrected the technology table to show Amazon API Gateway's East-West Private endpoint role alongside North-South; scoped the remaining unqualified OTel mandate (Requirement Category 3) to Kubernetes/EKS; made the API catalog OpenAPI-reference practice style-neutral | PR #249 review remediation, round 2 |
| 2026-09-10 | 1.0.2 | GitHub Copilot | Split mandatory requirements by actual source compliance tier; resolved East-West traffic conflict with the active AWS security SBB (Private API Gateway mandatory baseline, service mesh complementary); scoped OTel requirement to Kubernetes/EKS and corrected the Dynatrace/CloudWatch backend hierarchy | PR #249 review remediation |
| 2026-07-24 | 1.0.1 | GitHub Copilot | Clarified security and governance guidance after review feedback | Documentation maintenance |
| 2026-07-14 | 1.0.0 | GitHub Copilot | Initial standard profile creation | New standard profile |
